evidence.scope: Let a delivered ticket be reopened before its work is merged: void the receipt with a recorded reason, return the ticket to tdd on a new attempt, and refuse once the delivered commit is in the default branch.
acceptance: reopen on a delivered ticket appends a reopen record carrying the voided receipt hash, the reason and the actor, and status shows tdd on the next attempt: evidenced by the record and its test
reopen on a ticket that is not delivered is refused, naming the stage it is in: evidenced by the test
reopen after the delivered commit reached the default branch is refused, naming the merge: evidenced by a test that merges the commit first
verify-delivery after a reopen writes a second receipt and doctor still verifies the chain: evidenced by the test that walks a ticket through twice
A voided receipt is never deleted or rewritten: evidenced by the chain verifying across the reopen
decisions: A receipt is final when the work is merged, not when it is written. SEEN-086 made delivered terminal on the opposite assumption, and two tickets found defects after their receipts, each patched on the branch so the receipt attested a commit that was not the one merging. Founder, 23 September 2026
Reopening is refused once the commit is an ancestor of the default branch: a merged receipt is history, and history is not edited
The reopen record follows the receipt rather than replacing it, so the journal reads receipt, void, rework, second receipt, and SEEN-091 can count the rework where it happened
This is new capability rather than a correction of SEEN-088, which is why it is its own ticket rather than a patch on an open branch
graph_impact: verify-delivery in harness/delivery.py writes the receipt and is what reopen voids
journal.state applies the last transition, so a reopen record is read the same way an advance or a return is
